title: 5 Best Bookshop Cafés in Samcheong-dong 2026
description: The best bookshop cafés in Samcheong-dong & Bukchon, Seoul — curated from Reddit reviews and travel blogs. Hanok book cafés, mountain retreats & literary hideaways.

places.name: BooksCooks (북스쿡스)
places.whatToOrder: A scone with tea — their baked goods are exceptional. Browse the curated cookbook collection while you eat. The space doubles as a small restaurant with seasonal menus.

redditQuotes.text: We recommend BooksCooks, where you can dine surrounded by walls of cookbooks and literature in a beautifully renovated hanok.
The decor is very unique, incorporating a bit of vintage and modern in a renovated hanok — very cute and cozy, but surprisingly roomy inside.

places.insiderTip: Tucked into the alleys of Bukchon Hanok Village, BooksCooks is the kind of place you stumble upon and immediately fall in love with. The hanok architecture, carefully curated book collection, and excellent food make it feel like visiting a well-read friend's home. Perfect after exploring Bukchon's narrow streets.

places.name: Dae-o Bookstore (대오서점)
places.whatToOrder: A simple coffee in the adjacent café area. The real draw is the atmosphere — shelves packed with secondhand Korean literature, faded covers, and decades of literary history.

redditQuotes.text: I went to Namjoon (RM from BTS)'s favourite bookstore café, Dae-o Bookstore in Seoul. It's been open since 1951 and it's magical.

places.insiderTip: Seoul's oldest bookstore, open since 1951, sits in the heart of Seochon — a 10-minute walk from Samcheong-dong through Gyeongbokgung. Cash only, tiny, and gloriously unchanged. BTS's RM made it famous internationally, but locals have loved it for decades. The café extension adds just enough comfort without disturbing the old-world charm. Open daily 12:00–21:00.

places.name: The Forest Chosochaekbang (더숲 초소책방)
places.whatToOrder: The signature Ang butter croissant (red bean and butter) with artisanal coffee. Grab a book on environmental topics from their curated collection and sit by the glass walls overlooking Seoul.

redditQuotes.text: The Forest Chosochaekbang is housed in a former security guard post on Inwangsan Mountain. Glass walls, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, panoramic city views. One of the most unique cafés in Seoul.

places.insiderTip: A former police guard post reborn as a glass-walled book sanctuary on Inwangsan Mountain. The 20-minute uphill walk from Gyeongbokgung through Seochon village is part of the experience — you'll pass Tongin Market and the Yun Dong-ju Literature Museum. Specializes in environmental literature and hosts intimate book talks and music concerts. Worth the climb.

places.name: My Book Café (마이북카페)
places.whatToOrder: A cappuccino — their foam is legendarily rich, almost like whipped cream. Browse the floor-to-ceiling walls of books while you wait. Most are in Korean, but the atmosphere transcends language.

redditQuotes.text: I'm also a big fan of the Book Cafe. The place has walls of books and you can browse through any of the books there. I had a wonderful cappuccino that had foam so rich it could have been whipped cream.

places.insiderTip: The OG Samcheong-dong book café — right on the main café street. Walls lined floor-to-ceiling with books create a cozy, library-like atmosphere. The cappuccino is genuinely excellent. A perfect pit stop during a Samcheong-dong walk. No pretension, just good coffee and good books.

places.name: Café Yeon (카페 연)
places.whatToOrder: Traditional Korean tea — they have an excellent selection including citron (yuja) tea and jujube tea. The warm drinks complement the hanok atmosphere perfectly.

redditQuotes.text: Yeon is the hippie café where the servers don't wear shoes even in the dead of winter and the interior has a traditional hanok style, but like it has been refinished and repainted for modern times. The entire place induces a calming sigh. It's a bit of peace in the hectic world of Seoul.

places.insiderTip: Not a traditional bookshop café, but Café Yeon belongs on this list for its literary atmosphere and zen-like reading vibe. The renovated hanok on an elevated walkway near the Samcheong-dong toy museum is the most peaceful spot in the neighborhood. Bring your own book, order tea, and disappear for a few hours. This is what slow travel feels like.
